question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite $\sqrt[4]{e}$ as a power of $e$ (the base of the natural logarithm) as follows:

$$
\sqrt[4]{e}={e}^{1/4}
$$

Therefore, we have:

$$
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt[4]{e})=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{1/4})
$$

The natural logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x})=x
$$

In our case, we have $x=\frac{1}{4}.$ Therefore:

$$
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{1/4})=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{8}
$$
